title: Finance: Budgeting & Forecasting, Procurement, Contracts, and Revenue Recognition - Policy and Procedures
author: Monica Alvarez
content:
Overview

This document defines Redwood Inference's operating policy and standard procedures for: budgeting & forecasting, procurement, contract review and execution, and revenue recognition & billing. It is intended for finance, legal, procurement, product, and engineering managers who participate in budget planning, vendor selection, contract negotiation, and revenue reporting.

Scope
- Applies to all Redwood entities and global regions unless a customer-specific or legal jurisdictional requirement overrides these standards.
- Covers: annual budgeting, quarterly reforecasts, purchase approvals, vendor onboarding, contract intake & review, signature authority, and revenue recognition for hosted, dedicated, and private offerings.

Owner & Contacts
- Policy Owner: Finance (Monica Alvarez, Head of FP&A)
- Contract Intake: Legal (Contracts@redwood.example.com)
- Procurement & Vendor Management: Procurement Team (procurement@redwood.example.com)
- Billing & RevRec: Revenue Operations (revops@redwood.example.com)

1) Budgeting & Forecasting

Objective
- Produce an accurate, auditable plan that aligns headcount, cloud/GPU spend, and go-to-market investments with company strategy and revenue targets.

Cadence & Deliverables
- Annual Operating Plan (AOP): detailed budget by cost center due Nov 15 for the following fiscal year.
- Quarterly Rolling Forecast: updated revenue and spend forecast within 10 business days after quarter close.
- Monthly Actuals vs Forecast: variance analysis for significant deviations (>5% of line item or >$50k).

Roles & Responsibilities
- Finance (FP&A): coordinate AOP, consolidate organizational budgets, run scenario modeling, and validate assumptions.
- Managers: submit budget requests with clear justification (headcount plan, variable costs, capital requests).
- Engineering/Product Leaders: provide workload and capacity plans (GPU, storage, egress) with cost estimates based on platform telemetry.

Required Inputs & Assumptions
- Headcount plan (FTE count, role, base comp band, hiring phasing)
- Infrastructure run-rate: baseline GPU hours, reserved capacity commitments, cloud egress forecasts
- Sales bookings & ARR pipeline by cohort, churn assumptions, and average contract value (ACV) by segment

Approval Workflow
1. Manager-level submission to finance via Budget Intake form (NetSuite/Confluence link).
2. FP&A review and consolidation.
3. Executive review (CFO + relevant ELT members).
4. Final sign-off by CFO.

2) Procurement Procedures

Procurement Goals
- Minimize spending leakage, standardize vendor terms, and ensure vendors meet security and compliance requirements.

Vendor Categories & Approval Thresholds
| Spend Tier | Approval Required | Procurement Involvement | Notes |
|-----------:|------------------|------------------------|-------|
| <$5,000 | Manager | Optional | Local ad-hoc purchases (credit card).
| $5,000 - $150,000 | Finance Manager + Procurement | Recommended | Standard SOW or subscription; procurement negotiates pricing.
| >$50,000 | Director Finance/CFO + Procurement + Legal | Required | Capital or multi-year commitments; budget hold required.

Vendor Onboarding Checklist
- Vendor risk assessment (security questionnaire) - Security team approval required for vendors with data access.
- W-9/W-8 collection and tax status verification.
- Execute vendor master record in ERP (NetSuite).
- Procurement negotiates payment terms (standard: Net 30), discounts, and termination clauses.

Purchase Order (PO) Process
1. Requester creates PO request in procurement system with cost center and GL code.
2. Procurement validates vendor, pricing, and T&Cs.
3. Finance approves PO for budgets > threshold.
4. PO issued to vendor; goods/services accepted before invoice match.

3) Contracts & Legal Process

Objective
- Ensure consistent, low-risk contract terms and timely review cycles so product and sales can operate without unnecessary legal bottlenecks.

Contract Intake & Triage
- All contract requests must go through the Contract Intake Form (DocuSign/Confluence intake link). Include: counterparty, scope, MSA/SOW, term length, expected revenue or spend, and any data residency/processing needs.

Review SLAs & Timelines
- Standard SaaS/Hosted API MSA: target legal review turnaround = 3-15 business days.
- Custom terms or high-risk contracts (data processing, regulated customers): 7-15 business days.
- Sales enablement: priority intake for committed-revenue deals with signed term sheets - legal to triage same day.

Signature Authorities
- Up to $50k: Head of Business Unit or VP-level sign-off.
- $50k - $150k: CFO + Legal Countersignature.
- >$250k or strategic partnership: CEO + CFO + General Counsel.

Contract Redlines & Negotiation Guidelines (summary)
- Payment terms: default Net 30. Prefer to avoid advance payment beyond 30 days unless required by procurement.
- Liability cap: standard = limitation to fees paid in prior 12 months; exceptions require GC approval.
- Data Processing Agreement (DPA): required for any customer/vendor processing personal data. Use standard Redwood DPA template.
- Subcontracting: require disclosure and flow-down obligations for critical subprocessors.

Contract Execution Checklist
1. Intake form submitted and intake ID assigned.
2. Verify budget/ACV and PO (if customer is paying upfront).
3. Legal review and redline iteration recorded in the contract tracker.
4. Signatures collected via DocuSign.
5. Store fully executed agreement in contract repository (SharePoint/DocuSign storage) and create vendor/customer record in NetSuite.

4) Revenue Recognition & Billing Policy

Accounting Framework
- Redwood follows ASC 606 revenue recognition principles: identify contract(s), performance obligations, transaction price, allocate price to obligations, and recognize as obligations are satisfied.

Product-specific Rules
- Hosted API (Usage-based): recognize revenue as services are delivered (as tokens are consumed). For invoiced usage, record revenue in the period of usage; create accruals/deferrals for estimated usage not yet invoiced at period close.
- Dedicated (Reserved Capacity): for committed monthly/annual capacity with upfront prepayment, recognize revenue ratably over the committed period unless performance obligations are completed at a different pattern (document rationale).
- Private Deployments & Licensing: perpetual licenses recognized on delivery/transfer of control; maintenance and support recognized ratably over contract term.

Invoicing & Billing Controls
- Standard billing cadence: monthly in arrears for usage-based customers; monthly or annual invoicing for committed contracts depending on contract terms.
- Payment terms: standard Net 30; negotiated terms documented in contract and reflected in AR aging.
- Billing toolchain: Stripe (card payments), NetSuite (invoicing & AR), and custom billing pipeline for usage mediation.

Deferred Revenue & Cutover Controls
- Deferred revenue must be recorded for cash received in advance and released on the same basis as revenue recognition schedule.
- Quarterly review of deferred revenue schedules by RevOps and Accounting; exceptions documented and escalated.

Revenue Cutover Example (Reserved Capacity)
- Customer prepays $120k for a 12-month reserved capacity contract starting July 1.
- Accounting entry on receipt: Debit Cash $120k / Credit Deferred Revenue $120k.
- Monthly recognition from July 1: Debit Deferred Revenue $10k / Credit Revenue $10k.

Credit & Collections
- AR aging reviewed weekly by RevOps.
- Overdue >30 days: automated reminders. >60 days: account owner escalation to Sales + RevOps. >90 days: collections team involvement and potential suspension of service per contract.
- Late fee policy: interest per contract terms (default 1.5% per month) after 30 days unless prohibited by law or customer contract.

5) Controls, Audit & Reporting

Control Activities
- Segregation of duties: procurement cannot both create vendor invoice and approve payment for the same vendor.
- Contract repository and AR system reconciled monthly.
- PR/PO matching enforced for purchases over $5,000.

Audit & Evidence Requirements
- Maintain documentation for all material contracts, PO approvals, vendor security attestations, and billing reconciliations for at least 7 years.
- Support external audits (SOX or SOC) with evidence packages per auditor requests - FP&A & Legal are primary contacts.

Key Metrics & Dashboards (owned by Finance/RevOps)
- Deferred revenue balance (monthly)
- Days Sales Outstanding (DSO) and AR aging buckets
- Budget variance % by cost center (monthly)
- Contract turnaround time (intake -> fully executed)
- Vendor spend concentration (top 10 vendors)

Appendices
A. Standard Templates & Links
- Budget Intake Form: /confluence/finance-and-legal/budgeting-and-forecasting/budget-intake-form
- Contract Intake & Templates: /confluence/finance-and-legal/contracts-and-legal-process/contract-intake-templates
- Vendor Security Questionnaire: /confluence/security-and-compliance/vendor-security-questionnaire
- Revenue Recognition Accounting Matrix (detailed journal entries): /confluence/finance-and-legal/revrec-and-billing/revrec-accounting-matrix

B. Quick Reference: Approval Thresholds
- <$5k: Manager sign-off
- $5k - $150k: Finance Manager + Procurement
- $50k - $150k: CFO + Legal countersignature
- >$250k: CEO + CFO + GC

C. Escalation Paths
- Procurement disputes: Procurement -> Finance Director -> CFO
- Contract legal risk: Legal Counsel -> General Counsel -> CEO (if >$250k or material legal exposure)
- Revenue recognition judgment: RevOps -> Head of Accounting -> CFO -> External auditor (if unresolved)

Revision History
- 2024-02-15: Document created (Monica Alvarez).
- 2024-11-10: Updated procurement thresholds (Procurement team).
- 2025-09-20: Clarified revenue recognition treatment for reserved capacity and updated tooling references (RevOps).

Notes & Implementation Guidance
- Teams implementing these procedures should reference the linked templates and coordinate with the named owners. Exceptions to policy must be documented and approved in writing by the CFO and GC.

End of document.
